headline: Variances for 104 Lincoln Street addition, allowing 7.67-foot side yard and 37 percent coverage, approved.
summary: The owners built a bedroom and full bathroom on the lower level for Colleen's mother, who moved in after her husband died. A survey showed the addition is 7.67 feet from the side yard line, where 12 feet is required. The applicants' attorney said a contractor's miscalculation caused the problem. The board also denied a variance for 86 Desa Drive without prejudice because the applicant was not present.
decisions: Denied without prejudice a side yard variance at 86 Desa Drive, because the applicant was not present and 35 days had passed.
Approved variance for 104 Lincoln Street addition, with a 7.67-foot side yard setback and 37 percent coverage.
discussion: 104 Lincoln Street variance: Members debated whether a contractor's error can count as a hardship. Some said the narrow lot and the need for a bedroom and bathroom on the lower level supported the variance. The applicants' attorney said the survey showed 37 percent coverage, above the 30 percent allowed.

Survey requirements for applications: Members discussed asking for a survey on variance requests, because assessor and GIS maps are not precise. Members said a survey can be costly, and that an as-built survey is usually needed before a certificate of occupancy.

Certificate of occupancy: Members asked what happens if an owner-occupied home has no certificate of occupancy. The answer given was that open permits can cause problems when the owner sells or refinances.

Member recruitment and training: Members discussed a town fair as a place to recruit members, and asked for an update at the next meeting. They also asked about training events in the area for the coming year.
